lettet.explanation: "Lettet" means "relieved". To say what you are relieved about, use "over" (about): "Jeg er lettet over, at eksamen er overstået" (I am relieved that the exam is over).

levedygtig.explanation: "Levedygtig" means "viable". It is built from "at leve" (to live) and "dygtig" (skilled). To say a company can keep going, say: "Firmaet er levedygtigt" (The company is viable).

levende.explanation: "Levende" means "living". It comes from the verb "at leve" (to live). To say music is played live, use it for "live": "levende musik" (live music).

leverpostej.explanation: "Leverpostej" means "liver pâté". It is built from "lever" (liver) and "postej" (pâté). To talk about the warm kind, say: "lun leverpostej med bacon" (warm liver pâté with bacon).

liberal.explanation: "Liberal" means "liberal". To describe a relaxed way of raising children, say: "en liberal opdragelse" (a relaxed upbringing). A fact about Denmark: the party "Venstre" (literally "left") is a liberal party.

lidenskab.explanation: "En lidenskab" means "a passion". To say you do something with great feeling, use "med lidenskab" (with passion): "Hun spiller med lidenskab" (She plays with passion).

lidenskabelig.explanation: "Lidenskabelig" means "passionate". It is built from "en lidenskab" (a passion). To say someone cares deeply about a subject, say: "Hun har en lidenskabelig interesse for kunst" (She has a passionate interest in art).

lidt.explanation: "Lidt" means "a little". To say you want a small amount of something, put it before the thing: "lidt mælk" (a little milk). To say you are slightly tired, put it before the describing word: "lidt træt" (a little tired). Do not mix it up with "lille" (small): "en lille kop" (a small cup) is about size, while "lidt vand" (a little water) is about amount.

lidt efter lidt.explanation: "Lidt efter lidt" means "little by little". Literally, it is "a little after a little". To say how you learn a language, say: "Hun lærer dansk lidt efter lidt" (She learns Danish little by little).

lidt langsommere, tak.explanation: "Lidt langsommere, tak" means "a bit slower, please". "Langsommere" means "slower" and comes from "langsom" (slow). To ask someone to say it once more, ask: "Kan du sige det igen?" (Can you say that again?)

lige.explanation: "Lige" means "straight". To point to the exact moment or place, it means "right": "lige nu" (right now) and "lige ved siden af" (right next to).

lige meget hvad.explanation: "Lige meget hvad" means "no matter what". To promise someone help, say: "Jeg hjælper dig, lige meget hvad" (I will help you, no matter what). It is built from "lige meget" (it does not matter) and "hvad" (what).

lige nu.explanation: "Lige nu" means "right now". It is built from "lige" (just) and "nu" (now). To say something happens in a little while instead, use "om lidt" (in a little while): "Jeg kommer om lidt" (I am coming in a little while).

lige om lidt.explanation: "Lige om lidt" means "in just a moment". It is built from "om lidt" (in a little while) and "lige" (just).

ligefrem.explanation: "Ligefrem" means "downright". To stress that something is very much so, put it before the describing word: "Det er ligefrem fantastisk" (It is downright fantastic). To say a person is direct and simple, use it for "straightforward": "en ligefrem mand" (a straightforward man).

ligeglad.explanation: "Ligeglad" means "indifferent". To say you do not mind which choice is made, say: "Jeg er ligeglad" (I do not mind). To say someone does not care about other people, add "med" (about): "Han er ligeglad med andre" (He does not care about other people).

ligegyldig.explanation: "Ligegyldig" means "unimportant". To say something does not matter, say: "Det er ligegyldigt" (It makes no difference). To say a person does not care, use it for the person: "Hun virker ligegyldig" (She seems indifferent).

ligeledes.explanation: "Ligeledes" means "likewise". To answer a greeting with the same, reply: "Rart at møde dig!" "Ligeledes!" (Nice to meet you! Likewise!)

ligesom.explanation: "Ligesom" means "just like". It is built from "lige" (just) and "som" (like). To compare two people, put it before the second one: "Hun er høj ligesom sin mor" (She is tall just like her mother).

ligestilling.explanation: "Ligestilling" means "equality". It is built from "lige" (equal) and "en stilling" (a position). To talk about equal treatment at work, say: "ligestilling på arbejdspladsen" (equality in the workplace).

ligeså.explanation: "Ligeså" means "just as". To say two things are equal, put it before the describing word: "Hun er ligeså høj som dig" (She is just as tall as you). You can also write it as two words with the same meaning: "lige så høj" (just as tall).

ligeud.explanation: "Ligeud" means "straight ahead". To tell someone to go another way, use "til højre" (to the right) or "til venstre" (to the left): "Du skal til højre ved krydset" (You must go right at the intersection).

ligeværdig.explanation: "Ligeværdig" means "equal". It is built from "lige" (equal) and "værd" (worth). To say two sides count the same, say: "Vi er ligeværdige parter" (We are equal parties).

lignende.explanation: "Lignende" means "similar". To say a problem is alike another one, put it before the noun: "et lignende problem" (a similar problem). To say one person looks like another, use "ligner" (looks like): "Han ligner sin far" (He looks like his father).

lilla.explanation: "Lilla" means "purple". To say a lighter shade, put "lys" (light) in front of it: "lyslilla" (light purple).
